read_documentation.rationale: No SECRET/UNTRUSTED/SINK label: the tool is advertised to `Fetch and convert an AWS documentation page` and the URL requirements say it `Must be from the docs.aws.amazon.com domain` and `Must end with .html`, so it is limited to public AWS documentation rather than attacker-chosen hosts, local/intranet resources, or attacker-authored content.

read_sections.rationale: The tool `Retrieves a page, converts to markdown, and returns only matching sections`, but its stated URL requirement is only `Must end with .html`; unlike other tools, it does not state that the URL must be on `docs.aws.amazon.com`. Under the least restrictive reading, an agent-chosen `.html` URL could be an attacker-controlled web page, making returned markdown UNTRUSTED; it could be a `localhost` or intranet URL, making returned content SECRET; and fetching an agent-chosen URL can make a request to an attacker-readable host, making it a SINK. This is undetermined because the prose also says `AWS documentation pages`, but the advertised URL requirements do not settle the host restriction.

search_table.rationale: No SECRET/UNTRUSTED/SINK label: the tool searches a table on an `AWS documentation page URL` and the URL requirements say it `Must be from the docs.aws.amazon.com domain` and `Must end with .html`, so it does not advertise access to local/private resources or attacker-chosen hosts. Returned table data is from AWS documentation, not attacker-authored content under the threat model.

search_documentation.rationale: No SECRET/UNTRUSTED/SINK label: it searches `AWS documentation using the official AWS Documentation Search API` and returns AWS documentation `search_results` such as `url`, `title`, `context`, `recommended_sections`, and `sections`. A query to this fixed official AWS endpoint is not an attacker-readable destination, and the advertised results are official AWS documentation rather than attacker-controlled content.

recommend.rationale: No SECRET/UNTRUSTED/SINK label: it is advertised to `Get content recommendations for an AWS documentation page` and returns `recommended pages with URLs, titles, and context`. The description does not say it fetches the supplied URL as an agent-chosen host, and the returned recommendations are AWS documentation pages, not attacker-authored content under the threat model.

notes: No source code was provided; judgments are based only on the advertised tool names, descriptions, schemas, and annotations.
